data.name: AlHussein
data.gender_notes: AlHussein is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: AlHussein is the grandson of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). He is known for his courage, sacrifice, and loyalty. AlHussein is the third imam of Shia Muslims and the tenth imam of Sunni Muslims. The name AlHussein carries the meaning “Grandson of Prophet Muhammad” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose AlHussein usually hope their child will grow to embody grandson of prophet muhammad and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of sacrifice and loyalty to faith and family.
data.etymology: AlHussein belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Grandson of Prophet Muhammad.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of AlHussein total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: AlHussein is a significant figure in Islamic history and culture, especially for Shia Muslims. He is revered for his loyalty and bravery, as he tried to uphold the rightful claim to the caliphate after the death of his father, Ali. The Battle of Karbala, in which AlHussein and his companions were martyred, is a symbol of the struggle for justice and the innocence of the oppressed. This Day of Ashura, commemorating AlHussein's martyrdom, is an important religious event for Shia Muslims with various cultural practices and rituals.
data.spiritual_significance: AlHussein is considered a paragon of martyrdom and devotion. His life and death serve as enduring reminders of the perseverance, self-sacrifice, and unwavering commitment to faith required of believers. Moreover, his legacy extends beyond the religious sphere, as he is also considered an exemplar of leadership, sacrifice, and unwavering devotion to the truth. AlHussein's martyrdom has inspired generations of devotees, and his message of hope, justice, and self-sacrifice resonates deeply within Islamic spirituality.
